claim: Memory, planning, reflection and tool use have been copied into agents widely, but control couplings (typed impasse, commitment, resource-bounded stopping) are uneven or missing; this rests on one review with one coder and no experiment. Gap pass: a 48-author 2025 survey (d20) was only skimmed and gave no independent coding.
agent_test: Not testable directly; test each residual bundle separately (K04, K15).

claim: Reflection and self-correction help only when the success signal is reliable and external (unit tests, oracle label, environment state). Without it, accuracy stays flat or falls. Gap pass adds: sound verifier lifts Game of 24 3 to 38 and graph coloring 2 to 37 while GPT-4 self-critique lowers both (d01); tool beats no-tool in CRITIC (d09); math Self-Refine gains 0 to 0.2 (d08).
agent_test: Equal tokens: scaffold with code-run check vs same loop with model-only critique; report round-by-round accuracy.
audit_note: Self-critique lowered Game of 24 and coloring, but Blocksworld rose 40 to 55, so the claim holds only for the two domains it names.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction lowers accuracy on reasoning tasks for 2023-24 models (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after five calls; Gemini 1.5 Flash MATH -11.2 points from first to second attempt, d07). Oracle labels lift GPT-4 to 97.5 GSM8K and 59.0 HotpotQA. Independent replications now exist (Stechly, Kumar). Not yet measured with 2025-26 reasoning models.
agent_test: Replicate on current reasoning models; see K17 for what is known on them.
audit_note: Numbers match Huang Tables 2-3, Stechly, SCoRe; 'not yet measured with 2025-26 reasoning models' is an absence claim not checkable here; SCoRe is Google DeepMind like Huang, though different authors.

claim: A typed recovery step on failure (Soar-like impasse, then scoped sub-problem) is only partly implemented in agents; no system composes typed impasse, isolated substate, typed return and compile. Gap pass found no measurement of an impasse-triggered scoped sub-call against plain retry at equal tokens (gap 1 stays open); closest equal-budget evidence is d10 and d14.
agent_test: Add an impasse trigger (no candidate, tie, stuck) that opens a scoped sub-call and compare to plain retry and to self-consistency at equal tokens.

claim: Using the LLM as a knowledge source checked by symbolic code before use beats raw prompting: over 70% of raw responses were unusable for an embodied agent; STARS 77.5/94.4/92.9% vs template 52.5/66.7/35.7%.
agent_test: Model proposes, code validates; compare to unchecked use on the same tasks.
audit_note: Numbers match Kirk et al. Table 2 (STARS 77.5/94.4/92.9 vs TBP 52.5/66.7/35.7; over 70% unviable in one task), but both supporting papers are the same Soar group (Kirk, Wray, Laird) and the evidence is one simulation study, one run per condition; Zhu and Simmons does not test this.

claim: Reusing experience from earlier episodes helps in Voyager (verified code skills), AWM (workflows from successful trajectories), ExpeL (text insights plus retrieved successes; ALFWorld 40.0 to 59.0, task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs random 42.5) and bootstrapped agents; Voyager's ablations show self-verification matters most, which suggests (not shown) that a cheap executable check is needed. Payback at equal total tokens is unmeasured; Laird 1986 chunking data unread.
agent_test: Cache verified solutions with conditions; measure gain on a second similar problem set at equal total tokens including caching cost.
audit_note: Numbers check out (ExpeL 40.0 to 59.0; task-similarity 59.0 vs random 42.5; Voyager; AWM +12.0 pts), but no source tests the 'only where a cheap executable check exists' condition, and ExpeL stores text insights and trajectories, not compiled rules or code.
claim_before_audit: Compiling verified solutions into reusable rules or code (chunking analogue) is supported by Voyager, AWM, ExpeL and bootstrapped agents, but only where a cheap executable check exists. ExpeL: ALFWorld 40 to 59, task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs random 42.5 (d19). Payback at equal total tokens is still unmeasured; Laird 1986 chunking data still unread.

claim: In Zhu and Simmons, bootstrapped rules removed LLM calls on repeated tasks (15/15 without LLM on some tasks) and cut test cost from about 120 to under 40 dollars; steps did not differ significantly (p=0.446, 0.347). Token columns are garbled and unreliable.
agent_test: Small kitchen simulator, 15 trials per cell; reproduce on a text task suite.

claim: Program-driven search (Tree of Thoughts, LATS) lifts puzzle tasks far above CoT (Game of 24: 4% vs 74% at b=5) but costs many more calls. At matched budgets, self-consistency regularly beats ToT, Reflexion and debate on 6 datasets (d10); MCTS under-performs sampling at equal FLOPs on MATH (d13); on web tasks search beats reranking but costs up to 20 times the calls (d12). Edge over best-of-N at equal tokens is small or negative outside puzzles with strong value functions.
agent_test: Give ToT and best-of-N equal token budgets on the same non-puzzle items.

claim: Reflexion does not always beat the base model: MBPP Python fell 80.1 to 77.1 with a 16.3% test false-positive rate (1.4% on HumanEval); without test generation, Rust fell to 52% vs 60% base. (Leetcode Hard was 7.5 to 15.0.) At a matched 20-query budget Reflexion was the worst of three strategies and lost to self-consistency (d10).
agent_test: Measure the false-positive rate of our checks and gate reflection on it.

claim: The long-term memory plus reflection plus planning stack raises rated believability in simulated social agents (TrueSkill 29.89 full vs 21.21 none; d=8.16 vs prior work) but this is not task success.
agent_test: Do not cite as evidence for problem-solving gain.

claim: Paged outside memory raises deep memory retrieval (GPT-4 32.1 to 92.5%) on a task built by the authors against a truncation baseline. Independent benchmark (MemoryAgentBench, d17) finds long context best overall (60.6) and agentic memory systems worse, so the MemGPT gain is relative to truncation only.
agent_test: Test only if our tasks exceed context; gate on equal tokens (G7).

claim: An LLM-generated problem spec without search control costs orders of magnitude more solver steps; an execution-grounded critic is the most valuable part of an LLM-to-Soar-rule pipeline (-23% overall, -37% hard when removed). Gap 9 (spec with vs without search control in prompt scaffolds) found no direct study.
agent_test: Preliminary, one group each; ablate the critic in our own loop.

claim: Injecting ACT-R traces into an LLM by fine-tuning helped on a narrow choice task (accuracy 0.6576 vs 0.3564) but failed on multi-facet targets (0.42).
agent_test: Not a scaffold method; low priority.

claim: Learned memory managers (Memory-R1, AgeMem) and meta-agent search (ADAS) gain on benchmarks but need RL training or design-time search, outside our no-training scope. SCoRe (d07) is a further trained example.
agent_test: Out of scope (section 4b); cite only as upper-bound context.

claim: A commitment and reconsideration step in ReAct-style loops is proposed as a design pattern but nobody has measured it at equal tokens. Gap pass found none either (gap 2 stays open). Nearest measurement: bounded 'Wait' continuation in a reasoning model, AIME24 50.0 to 56.7 with 4 Waits and flattening after (d16).
agent_test: Test commit/reconsider vs plain ReAct at equal tokens.

claim: ReAct alone is not best on knowledge QA: HotpotQA ReAct 27.4 EM vs CoT 29.4, CoT-SC 33.4, hybrids 34.2-35.1; its gain is on state-tracking tasks (ALFWorld best 71% vs Act 45%).
agent_test: Hybrid with self-consistency is a candidate arm.

claim: On non-reasoning models the self-correction blind spot is large (64.5% average across 14 models; own errors caught 4.3-10.8%). Reasoning-trained models (R1 style) show almost none, and appending 'Wait' lifts DeepSeek-V3-0324 from 0.567 to 0.902 vs R1-0528 0.908. But reflection words in R1-Zero do not imply higher accuracy (nearly half of reflective answers no better). So an outer reflect loop adds less on reasoning models; a bounded nudge is the cheap form.
agent_test: Compare plain reasoning model, +Wait nudge, and outer critique loop at equal tokens on our tasks; score by wrong-to-right and right-to-wrong flips.

claim: Break-even reliability of an error finder is roughly 60 to 70% accuracy at locating the first wrong step (simulation, read from a figure); best 2023-24 LLM finder reached 52.87% (GPT-4 direct step-level). Below break-even, correction hurts right answers (0 to -11.43 points with oracle location). Not measured with reasoning models.
agent_test: Measure our check's false-positive and false-negative rates; allow reflection only above a measured gate; log flip rates.

claim: Selection is the bottleneck, not generation: coverage reaches 98.44% at 10,000 samples on MATH while majority vote and reward model stay near 41%; SWE-bench Lite rises 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples with a code-run verifier. A checker's reliability limits how much coverage can be used.
agent_test: Use executable checks to select among samples where available; otherwise do not expect gain beyond about 100 samples.

claim: Difficulty-aware allocation of test-time compute (sequential revision on easy items, mixed on hard, with a trained process reward model) matches best-of-N with up to 4 times less compute on MATH. Process-reward beam search degrades on easy items at large budgets.
agent_test: Test a difficulty-triggered switch between resample and revise at equal tokens; no trained reward model needed if a code check exists.

claim: Memory with activation-style scoring (ACT-R recency, frequency, context) has no measured edge over plain similarity retrieval in agent benchmarks found: BM25 60.5 beat Qwen3-Embedding-4B 54.7 on accurate retrieval, long context beat all agentic memory (d17), and Mem0 trails full context 66.88 vs 72.90 but uses about 15 times fewer tokens per query (d18). Anderson 2004 activation equation and fit numbers not read.
agent_test: Three-arm retrieval test at equal tokens: similarity only, similarity plus recency and frequency, and BM25.

claim: Search in the live environment helps web agents (VisualWebArena GPT-4o 18.9 to 26.4; budget c=0/5/20 gives 24.5/32.0/37.0) but costs up to 20 times more LM calls; value-function quality caps the gain (ground-truth reward 43.5 vs GPT-4o 20 samples 37.0). Destructive and irreversible actions are a failure mode.
agent_test: Only use search where actions are reversible or sandboxed; require value function accuracy check.
